extracted.intended_audience: photojournalists, journalists, media professionals, festival attendees, supporters of press freedom
extracted.subtask_description: An editorial piece by the festival director advocating for the role of professional journalism and photojournalism in the age of AI, and presenting the festival's scope and key figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reliable, up-to-date, verified data for AI models
rubrics_metrics.description: “These models, to be effective, must be fed reliable, up-to-date, and verified data.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial argues that news professionals are best suited to provide this verified data; notes the rapid formation of partnerships between large AI companies and established international press outlets as evidence of the value of verified journalistic data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to journalistic standards and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional journalists and media outlets publish work “that adhere to standards and rules that may be outdated, but are so important. And valuable.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece points to the continuing relevance of journalistic standards (verification, ethics, editorial oversight) and cites the success of The New York Times, Le Monde, and the Financial Times as proof of their ongoing value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media as bastions against misinformation and capture
rubrics_metrics.description: “With their influence, their legitimacy, and their power, they are the last bastions against the gravediggers of reality, who dream of only one thing: to tear them down or take them over to further their own agendas—and, above all, their business interests.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media organizations should resist political/technological pressures, mergers and acquisitions, or other forces that would undermine independent journalism; the editorial mentions taxpayer-funded investigative committees and commercial takeover as threats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defend values of freedom and journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: The festival and its community pledge to remain “faithful to the values of freedom and journalism.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continued public support and participation (e.g., at the festival in Perpignan) are framed as necessary to sustain journalistic freedoms and the festival’s mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographers' role in showing the world
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotation: “Photographers let me see what is happening in the world.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This asserts the essential function of photographers/photojournalists in documenting events and informing the public; implied criterion for valuing and selecting work is its ability to reveal and explain real-world events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of exhibitions per year
rubrics_metrics.description: “25+ exhibitions every year throughout the city of Perpignan.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a festival-scale metric indicating breadth of programming and public visibility across the city.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of awards and grants
rubrics_metrics.description: “17 awards and grants awarded to photojournalists.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantifies the festival’s support for photographers and can serve as an indicator of opportunities and recognition offered to practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evening screenings and audience size
rubrics_metrics.description: “6 evening screenings on a giant screen at the Campo Santo, attracting over 2,000 spectators each evening.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the festival’s public engagement and the scale of its showcase events; useful as a metric of impact and reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Countries represented
rubrics_metrics.description: “40+ countries represented through the exhibitions and reports.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals the festival’s international diversity and scope when evaluating its comprehensiveness and global reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of photojournalism reports
rubrics_metrics.description: “100+ photojournalism reports covering topics from all over the world.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflects the volume and topical breadth of work presented at the festival; can be used to assess program richness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total visits during the festival
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts as a quantitative measure of audience engagement and overall popularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Festival longevity / year founded
rubrics_metrics.description: “1989 – year the festival was founded” and “Over 30 editions covering the events that have shaped the world.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longevity is presented as evidence of established credibility, institutional memory, and continued relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of accredited professionals
rubrics_metrics.description: “1,000+ accredited professionals (photographers, editors, journalists, agencies...) every year.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the festival’s professional importance and networking value for practitioners; useful for assessing industry participation.
